activity.notes: Rakai Pikatan's exact accession is debated. Epigraphic scholarship shows that he was already king by 842 (possibly a few years earlier), while later inscriptional chronology places the succession to Rakai Kayuwangi around 855 and a 856 inscription already reflects the transition. ATLAS therefore uses c.842–c.855 rather than presenting a falsely precise reign.

sources.title: King Sanjaya and His Successors — Cornell University
sources.citation_text: The study argues from the 842 Sri Kahulunan charter that Rakai Pikatan must already have been king by 842.

sources.title: The Reliefs of Ramayana and Kṛṣṇa Story at Lara Jonggrang Temple and Reign Shift of the Ancient Mataram in 9th Century AD — Berkala Arkeologi
sources.citation_text: The Indonesian archaeological study notes that by the 856 Śivagṛha context Rakai Pikatan was no longer reigning and uses Wanua Tengah III in reconstructing the succession.
